guardrails.title: Use source-backed facts without redistributing upstream prose
rules: Prefer exact target-version data over latest-version data.
Do not fetch, crawl, summarize, or cite Minecraft Wiki pages in AI workflows; use source-policy/source-report to choose allowed sources.
Use Paper docs, Javadocs links, and allowed structured community datasets as provenance only within their documented source tier; do not copy or closely paraphrase upstream prose.
Treat null, unknown, seed, missing, not-extracted, or not-yet-published values as gaps, not facts.
When evidence is unavailable, state the gap instead of filling it from memory.
requiredEvidence: source-policy, source-report, or evidence bundle when citing provenance
target version detail or support entry when giving version-specific facts
guardrails.failureMode: Hallucinated facts, unsupported citations, or license-sensitive copied prose can enter generated output.

guardrails.title: Do not overstate datapack command and JSON evidence
rules: Command paths from server reports prove parser shape only; they do not prove gameplay behavior, permissions, or execution context.
Observed vanilla datapack JSON field paths are not normative schemas.
Do not infer required fields, optionality, or allowed custom extension behavior from observed vanilla files alone.
Do not reuse pack_format values or command syntax from neighboring versions without checking the target version.
requiredEvidence: server reports or command path search results for command syntax
observed datapack schema surface when discussing vanilla JSON field shapes
version detail packFormats.data for pack.mcmeta
guardrails.failureMode: Generated datapacks can contain commands or JSON shapes that look plausible but are not verified for the target version.

guardrails.title: Do not overstate resourcepack asset and model evidence
rules: Vanilla asset path matches prove bundled file paths only; they do not prove rendering behavior.
Observed model and item definition summaries do not prove every accepted key, required key, or rendering semantic.
Do not infer pack_format values or item model conventions from neighboring versions without checking the target version.
When a resource path is not found, do not invent a vanilla path.
requiredEvidence: vanilla path or inventory search results for asset paths
resourcepack model summary when discussing observed model or item definition fields
version detail packFormats.resource for pack.mcmeta
guardrails.failureMode: Generated resource packs can reference nonexistent vanilla paths or unverified model JSON conventions.

guardrails.title: Do not overstate Paper API surface evidence
rules: Paper support can lag the latest Java version; do not emit dependency coordinates for unsupported versions.
Javadocs package, type, and member indexes prove names and labels only.
Do not infer runtime behavior, overload semantics, nullability, thread safety, or Folia safety from a type/member match.
Event search results are candidates and must be verified against Paper/Bukkit API surfaces before generating listener code.
Flag Folia-sensitive scheduling and threading assumptions instead of silently using global scheduler patterns.
requiredEvidence: Paper project support metadata and Paper API reference for dependency coordinates
Paper Javadocs package/type/member surface for referenced API names
Paper event search result plus Javadocs confirmation for event candidates
Paper scheduler and Folia documentation links when code touches scheduling, worlds, entities, chunks, or async work
guardrails.failureMode: Generated plugins can compile against nonexistent APIs, target unsupported Paper versions, or hide unsafe threading assumptions.

guardrails.title: Preserve every item across partial inventory delivery
rules: Choose an explicit overflow policy before mutating a player's inventory: reject or defer the delivery, persist it for retry, or apply one verified fallback to the uninserted stacks.
When an inventory insertion API can return uninserted stacks, consume that result instead of treating the requested amount as fully delivered.
Account for inserted and uninserted stacks exactly once; never pass the original input to a fallback after a partial insertion.
If overflow is dropped, spawn only the uninserted stacks at the recipient's current world and location, and make the pickup or ownership policy explicit.
Verify every insertion, drop, ownership, or convenience member against the target Paper API and inspect behavior documentation before relying on its result contract.
Do not recommend Player.give or another convenience API for every Paper version; use it only when the target-version member and its overflow behavior are verified.
requiredEvidence: target-version Paper API type/member matches for every inventory insertion and selected fallback member
an explicit delivery result and overflow policy that accounts for every requested stack once
tests for complete insertion, partial insertion, full inventory, retry behavior, and selected fallback failure when applicable
guardrails.failureMode: A partially successful delivery can silently destroy leftover items or duplicate the portion already inserted when fallback or retry logic reuses the original input.

guardrails.title: Default-deny every interaction path in custom inventory GUIs
rules: Scope an owned GUI from the top inventory's stable holder or session identity; do not identify it only by mutable or shared title text.
For an owned view, cancel InventoryClickEvent and InventoryDragEvent before branching, then keep everything denied except an explicit slot-and-action allowlist.
Distinguish the top inventory, bottom player inventory, and outside clicks with the view, clicked inventory, and view-unique raw slots; a bottom-origin click can still modify the top inventory.
Deny shift-click and MOVE_TO_OTHER_INVENTORY by default because transfer starts in one inventory and targets the other.
Deny NUMBER_KEY, HOTBAR_SWAP, legacy HOTBAR_MOVE_AND_READD where present, and SWAP_OFFHAND unless the exact source and destination slots are deliberately modeled.
Deny DOUBLE_CLICK and COLLECT_TO_CURSOR by default because collection can inspect and remove matching items across the open view.
For InventoryDragEvent, allow a drag only when every raw slot in the complete footprint belongs to the allowed set; cancel the whole drag when any protected or unclassified slot is present.
Keep button clicks cancelled and apply GUI state changes manually; when changing event-affected slots, cancel first so the vanilla result cannot overwrite the change.

Do not use deprecated InventoryClickEvent.setCursor for manual cursor changes; verify a supported target-version mutation path and defer it when the event result can overwrite or desynchronize the cursor.
Choose whether every editable top inventory is per-session or deliberately shared, and define which player or transaction owns each editable stack before allowing insertion.

Settle editable top-inventory stacks exactly once when a session commits, closes, is replaced, disconnects, dies, or the plugin shuts down: atomically claim the open session, capture and clear or persist its owned stacks, and make repeated callbacks and queued tasks no-ops.

Choose an explicit overflow outcome when settled stacks cannot be returned to the player inventory; account for inserted and uninserted stacks exactly once instead of retrying or dropping the original amount.

Defer close, open, or reopen operations from InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, and InventoryCloseEvent handlers to the next target-compatible scheduler turn, then revalidate the player, current view, and GUI session before acting.

Do not force unconditional reopen loops after InventoryCloseEvent, and do not perform even a conditional reopen directly in that handler; handle close reason, disconnect, plugin shutdown, deliberate close, and replacement-view cases explicitly.
requiredEvidence: target-version Paper API type/member matches for InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, InventoryCloseEvent, InventoryView, ClickType, InventoryAction, close reason, and every cursor, settlement, insertion, or fallback member used by the handler
Paper event behavior documentation for cancellation, raw slots, deprecated cursor mutation, event-affected mutations, and close/open restrictions in click, drag, and close handlers

a project-specific matrix of owned views, per-session or shared ownership, top/bottom/outside regions, allowed slots, allowed click/action pairs, settlement outcomes, overflow policy, and deferred transition conditions

tests that exercise ordinary clicks, shift transfer, number-key and offhand swaps, double-click collection, cross-boundary drag, outside clicks, direct close-handler reopen rejection, deprecated cursor mutation rejection, editable-slot commit and return, full-inventory overflow, repeated close callbacks, disconnect, shutdown, and close/reopen races
guardrails.failureMode: A handler that cancels only obvious top-inventory clicks can be bypassed from the player inventory, cursor-wide collection, hotbar/offhand swaps, multi-slot drags, deprecated cursor mutation, duplicate settlement, unowned shared slots, or stale reopen tasks.

guardrails.title: Make administrative command surfaces operable and observable
rules: Inventory every operator action the feature needs: create or change, remove, inspect, reload, retry, repair, reset, unlock, or recover; provide a command path or document the intentional alternative for each required action.

Allow console execution whenever an operation does not require player-local input such as location, view, cursor, held item, or line of sight; provide explicit arguments alongside any player-context shortcut.

Enumerate dispatchable CommandSender subtypes available on the target Paper version, including player, local console, remote console, command block, command minecart, proxied, and custom senders; explicitly allow or reject each applicable kind, return feedback for rejection, and reject unknown or future subtype fallthrough by default.

Require an explicit target for privileged actions on a subject instead of silently treating the invoker as the target; decide online-only versus offline-capable resolution from the real state dependency.

Resolve an operator-facing player identifier to a stable stored identity, distinguish a known offline subject from unknown input, and do not treat an OfflinePlayer value by itself as proof that the subject is registered or has joined.
Attach an explicit least-privilege permission policy to every privileged branch and enforce it at execution; command visibility and filtered suggestions are not authorization.
Use typed, bounded arguments and explicit scope for bulk operations; require a preview, confirmation, or other deliberate acknowledgement before destructive or all-target mutation.

Do not accept raw secrets through command arguments or suggestions; use a protected secret, environment, or configuration path and keep values out of histories, logs, feedback, status output, and audit records.

For reload, parse and validate the complete candidate before atomically replacing effective state, preserve the last valid state on failure, and serialize or version concurrent reload and mutation work; keep file, database, and network I/O off the main server thread and publish Bukkit-facing state in a target-compatible execution context.
Return typed outcomes for success, missing target, invalid input or state, denial, partial completion, and I/O failure; do not hide expected operational results in exceptions or logs alone.
Report the result to the invoker, including console or an administrator acting on someone else, and treat notification of the affected target as a separate policy decision.

Provide list, show, or status output that reflects the effective post-change state without exposing secrets, and record security-sensitive changes with actor, target, action, result, and bounded non-secret context.

Test every supported and rejected sender kind, self and other targets, online and supported offline targets, permission denial, reload rollback, retry or idempotency, partial failure, bulk confirmation, and secret redaction.
requiredEvidence: an operation matrix mapping every required mutation, inspection, reload, recovery, and retry path to syntax or a justified safe alternative, sender kinds, permission, target kind, and outcomes
target-version Paper API type/member matches for command sender, player, offline-player, identity, permission, scheduler, and messaging APIs actually referenced
a state-transition design showing validation, atomic publication, last-known-good rollback, and concurrent reload or mutation handling
tests proving sender acceptance and rejection, target, permission, failure, observability, reload rollback, bulk-scope behavior, and secret redaction
guardrails.failureMode: An incomplete administrative command can force operators to edit files, restart servers, impersonate targets, or infer success from logs while unsafe sender, scope, permission, and reload paths remain untested.

guardrails.title: Separate stable player identity from mutable names and display output
rules: Use a stable player identifier backed by the authenticated identity boundary for persistence, ownership, joins, permissions, and references; account names and presentation labels are mutable attributes, not primary identity.

Document online mode, offline mode, and trusted proxy forwarding; do not treat every observed UUID as equally stable or authoritative. Direct offline mode needs an independently authenticated account link for rename-continuous identity; otherwise state that continuity is unavailable, forbid automatic name-based ownership remapping, and define migration if the identity mode changes.

Classify each player-related value as stable identity, lookup input, current account name, plugin-defined display label, or rendered Component or text instead of passing a generic name between layers.

Resolve human input through an explicit exact-match and normalization policy, and represent online, known offline, unknown, invalid, ambiguous when applicable, and lookup-unavailable outcomes separately.
Do not treat an OfflinePlayer object alone as evidence that a player is known, registered, or has joined.
Choose the intended label independently for every human-facing surface; never expose Player.name, OfflinePlayer.name, displayName, UUID, or a fallback chain merely because it is available.

Keep Component-based presentation distinct from plain account-name lookup and persistence values; treat untrusted names and labels as text rather than MiniMessage or other markup, and define allowed styling, click or hover events, null fallback, duplicate-label disambiguation, encoding, escaping, mention handling, newline and control-character handling, and plain-text serialization per transport.
Show UUIDs or historical names only for an explicit machine-integration, diagnostic, audit, or operator requirement, with an appropriate audience and privacy policy.
Perform profile, database, and network lookup off the main server thread with timeouts, bounded positive and negative caches, observable failure, and target-compatible Bukkit publication.

Define the authoritative source for each identity mapping, account-name attribute, and display label, plus an ordering, revision, or invalidation rule for join, rename discovery, profile update, reconnect, and cross-server propagation.

Test authenticated rename continuity or the explicit direct-offline limitation, known offline and unknown input, null names, duplicate, markup-like, mention-like, control-character, and event-bearing labels, stale caches, lookup timeout, reconnect, and every player-facing output transport in scope.
requiredEvidence: a value-flow table separating stable identity, lookup input, account name, display label, and rendered output
target-version Paper API type/member matches for Player, OfflinePlayer, profile, identity, lookup, and display APIs actually referenced

a persistence and resolution model that survives account-name changes only where an authenticated identity or independent account link supports it, records authentication or proxy-forwarding assumptions, and rejects unresolved identity
a per-transport presentation and fallback matrix
cache, threading, and cross-server convergence tests
guardrails.failureMode: Treating every player-related value as a name can attach data to the wrong identity, break after renames, expose internal identifiers, or render inconsistent labels across transports and servers.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper plugin-message and RPC protocol boundaries authenticated, bounded, and lifecycle-safe
rules: Use namespaced channels, register incoming and outgoing channels with explicit plugin lifecycle ownership, and unregister or release protocol state on disable.
Define a versioned envelope with explicit message kinds; reject unsupported versions, unknown kinds, malformed or truncated fields, trailing bytes, and non-canonical encodings.

Validate frame bytes, strings, collections, maps, nesting, declared decompressed sizes, derived totals, and every attacker-controlled allocation before allocating; cap and abort actual output while decompressing.
Handle the verified listener connection type and stage explicitly; a configuration-stage connection is not automatically an authenticated joined player.
Take the acting player and authorization context from the authenticated connection or an explicitly trusted proxy boundary, never from identity or permissions claimed by the payload.
Scope request IDs, duplicate detection, cancellation, and terminal-response state to one connection/session; define idempotency and emit at most one terminal response.
Clean pending requests, uploads, chunks, futures, and queued responses on timeout, cancellation, reconnect, connection close, and plugin disable.
Treat an eligible live connection or player as a required carrier; plugin messaging is not a durable standalone server transport, so closed or unavailable transport must have an explicit outcome.
Bound concurrent requests, chunks, uploads, queued bytes, decompressed bytes, and work; require chunk order, checksum, declared total size, completion, expiry, and backpressure.
Retry only operations explicitly declared idempotent, and keep transport decode/timeout/cancellation errors distinct from valid business outcomes.
Move blocking I/O and heavy decoding away from the server thread, then publish Bukkit state only from an execution context verified safe for the target API and scheduler model.
Verify target-version Messenger.MAX_CHANNEL_SIZE and Messenger.MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE when using them as transport ceilings, and apply explicit lower application budgets where needed.
StandardMessenger transport validation and documentation examples are necessary evidence where applicable but do not establish a complete safe application codec.
requiredEvidence: target-version Paper API type/member results and official documentation for channel registration, listener connection identity, byte-array sending, StandardMessenger validation, and Messenger size constants
protocol envelope, compatibility, authorization, idempotency, error, timeout, cancellation, retry, and lifecycle contracts
configured per-message, decoded, decompressed, collection, nesting, request, chunk, upload, queue, and concurrency budgets
hostile and boundary tests for decoding, spoofed identity, duplicates, stale sessions, timeouts, cleanup, chunk ordering/checksum/expiry, and backpressure
guardrails.failureMode: Untrusted payloads can cross authorization boundaries, exhaust memory or work budgets, replay side effects, leak per-connection state, or publish unsafe Bukkit mutations.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper connection-scoped work inside one player-session generation
rules: Separate durable player data from transient state owned by one accepted connection.
Identify a session by stable player identity plus an opaque session instance or generation and plugin lifecycle epoch, not by UUID alone.
Own tasks, subscriptions, listeners, pollers, UI viewers, cooldowns, caches, callbacks, reverse indexes, and references from one session ledger.
Use one idempotent close transition for quit, kick, relevant transfer, connection close, plugin disable or reload, failed or partial initialization, repeated signals, and reconciliation.
Dispose partial acquisitions in reverse order; continue clearing remaining resources and references when one cleanup action fails.
Do not retain Player references outside the live session boundary. Late async callbacks must reacquire a current target and verify session generation, plugin state, and required publication context.
Cancellation alone is not a publication fence; an already-running callback can still finish.
Order durable writes with revisions or idempotency keys and use bounded queues, retries, and flushes so an old session cannot overwrite newer state.
Close admission before plugin shutdown, wait behind an explicit bounded persistence barrier, and expose timeout or recovery state instead of starting fire-and-forget work after disable.
Verify target-version lifecycle event and scheduler APIs before naming them, do not assume every event fires in every phase, and provide a fallback reconciliation sweep.
Define transfer and reconnect semantics explicitly and observe active sessions, rejected stale publications, cleanup balance, reverse-index leaks, persistence age, and shutdown timeouts.
Keep item or inventory contents, ownership settlement, and transactional delivery outside this session-resource concern.
requiredEvidence: A durable-versus-transient state model and per-session resource ownership ledger
Target-version Paper type, member, event, and documentation evidence for the lifecycle surfaces actually used
An idempotent state machine, reverse-order rollback, generation and plugin-state publication fence, and reconciliation design
A revisioned persistence order and bounded shutdown-barrier contract
Race tests for rapid reconnect, stale completion, double cleanup, partial initialization, transfer, disable with in-flight persistence, and missing or late events
Leak metrics or structured logs plus a scope statement excluding inventory contents and settlement
guardrails.failureMode: Transient resources and callbacks can escape their connection generation, while unordered or unbounded shutdown writes corrupt durable player state.
